chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man upon whom fasting for a month was made obligatory, so he fasted fifteen days of it, then a matter presented itself preventing him, he said: If he had fasted fifteen days, then for him it is permissible to make up what remains, and if he had fasted less than fifteen days, it would not suffice for him until he fasts a complete month.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one is prevented from completing an obligatory month of fasting before reaching fifteen days?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between partial and complete fulfillment of a monthly fasting obligation, such as kaffarah or qada, when interrupted by a valid excuse. It establishes a critical threshold of fifteen days: if met, the obligation is reduced to the remainder; if not, the entire month must be restarted, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integrity of the continuous period (ittisal) in certain expiatory fasts. This ruling ensures that the spiritual and legal requirements of the vow or penalty are met with precision, avoiding ambiguity in religious practice.
